evals.name: rewrite-install-instructions
evals.prompt:
Rewrite this installation section from our pedestal meter manual in Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100). Keep it as markdown.

---
Installation

Prior to commencing installation, the installer should ensure that the upstream breaker has been de-energized and locked out, and that the absence of voltage has been verified at all terminals using a suitably rated meter; failure to do so could result in electric shock, severe injury or death. Mount the pedestal on the prepared concrete base utilizing the four M12 anchor bolts supplied, making sure the unit is level (adjust with shims if required), then torque the anchor bolts to 45 Nm. Feed the incoming supply cable through the bottom gland, strip approximately 15mm of insulation off each conductor and terminate L1, L2, L3 and N at the corresponding terminals as per the wiring diagram on the inside of the door, tightening each terminal screw to 2.5 Nm. The earth conductor must be connected to the earth bar before any other connection is made. Once all connections have been completed and checked, replace the cover, restore power at the upstream breaker and confirm that the display illuminates and shows the correct time; if it doesn't, refer to the troubleshooting section.

NOTE: Do not energise the unit with the cover removed.
evals.expected_output: A markdown rewrite: WARNING block(s) with command/condition then consequence; numbered single-action imperative steps each ≤20 words; no semicolons, no perfect tense, no -ing verbs, no non-approved words like ensure/verify/prior/commence/utilize/should/could; the NOTE converted to a step or safety instruction; brief STE compliance notes listing technical nouns.

evals.name: write-quickstart-from-notes
evals.prompt:
Write a one-page quick-start guide for installers for our new VoltSafe smart pedestal, following ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Here are the engineering notes to base it on:

- product: outdoor pedestal with integrated revenue-grade meter, 3-phase 400V, IP66 enclosure, powder coated steel, 1.2m tall
- comes with: 4x M12 anchor bolts, 2x cable glands (M40), keys, quick-start card
- install on level concrete base min 600x600x150mm, bolts torqued 45Nm
- supply cable enters through bottom gland; conductors 16-35mm2; terminal screws 2.5Nm; earth first
- after powering up the display shows the firmware version for 5 s then the home screen; green LED = OK, red LED flashing = fault, see manual
- commissioning: press and hold MENU 3 s to enter setup, set date/time and tariff, save with OK
- danger: live terminals behind cover, 400V. lockout upstream breaker before opening. don't hose the display directly.
- cleaning: mild detergent, soft cloth, no solvents

Produce it as markdown with headings.
evals.expected_output: A quick-start guide in STE: descriptive overview ≤25 words/sentence, WARNING/CAUTION blocks in the STE shape, numbered imperative steps ≤20 words, one action per step, condition-first sentences, approved vocabulary (make sure, set to OFF, push, etc.), product terms kept consistent, STE compliance notes with technical nouns listed.

evals.name: review-troubleshooting-text
evals.prompt:
Can you review this troubleshooting text against the ASD-STE100 rules and tell me what's wrong with it, rule by rule, then give me a corrected version?

If the meter fails to communicate with the head-end system, the first thing that should be checked is whether the RS-485 cable has been terminated properly at both ends, as improper termination is the most common cause of comms issues encountered in the field; a 120 ohm resistor needs to be fitted across A and B at the last device on the bus. Also check the polarity hasn't been reversed. When the fault persists after these checks have been carried out, power cycling the meter will usually clear it, however if it keeps happening the unit may need to be returned to VoltSafe for evaluation.
evals.expected_output: A rule-by-rule review citing STE rule numbers (8.1 semicolon, 3.4 perfect tenses, 3.6 passive, 3.5 -ing, 5.1/6.3 length, non-approved words check/should/properly/issues/fitted/needs/may/however with alternatives, 5.4 condition first, GR pronouns) followed by a corrected STE version with numbered steps.
